stem:
Heena and her uncle watch the clear night sky from a field near Shimla. He wants her to find North using familiar star patterns.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: The Pole Star is a member of the Big Dipper and slowly circles the sky each night.
The Pole Star belongs to the Little Dipper and appears nearly fixed, so it marks the North direction.
The brightest star they can see tonight must be the Pole Star and therefore marks North from any place on Earth.
The Big Dipper itself always sits due South, so it cannot help locate North.

teacher.key_rationale: Polaris is in the Little Dipper and appears nearly stationary in the northern sky, so finding it locates North when it is visible.
